_provenance.source: R ardlverse 2.0.0, panel_ardl(estimator=...), R 4.6.1, GPL-3. ardlverse states it replicates Stata's xtpmg (Blackburne & Frank 2007), the reference the spec designates; Stata is not available in this environment.
_provenance.data: tests/replication/data/spec23_panel.csv, versioned WITH the test (validation/ is gitignored, and a missing file would turn this regression test into a silent skip). Generated by validation/external/spec23_make_panel.py, seed 20260829. theta is COMMON (0.75) across individuals — the world PMG is specified for. Synthetic on purpose: no third-party dataset is redistributed.
_provenance.tolerance_note: The spec asks for 1e-3. Measured agreement at pyardl's DEFAULT settings (tol=1e-8) is 1.9e-08 on theta and 2.1e-10 on the standard error; with both sides fully converged it is 6.7e-10 and 7.7e-12. The contract is set at 1e-6: far tighter than the spec, loose enough to absorb the two stopping rules.
_provenance.reference_tolerance_note: ardlverse is run at tol=1e-10, NOT its default 1e-6. At the default it stops 2.7e-07 short of its own maximum — detected because the concentrated log-likelihood there is LOWER than at pyardl's estimate, not because the coefficients looked wrong. See OBS-21.
_provenance.convention_note: ardlverse writes the level term in x_{it}, the spec in x_{i,t-1}. The two parameterisations carry the SAME long-run theta (the short-run coefficients differ), which is why only theta, lambda and the log-likelihood are compared.
